title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow?

items.stem: Your assistant's booking path is Python code that always runs the same four steps: (1) a model call extracts machine, date and time from the student's message; (2) code calls check_calendar; (3) if the slot is free, code calls book_slot, otherwise code picks the next free slot; (4) a model call writes the confirmation. Which statement is right?

options.text: It is an agent: the model is called and tools are used along the way
It is a workflow: the code fixes the order, and the model handles only steps 1 and 4
It is an agent: the path changes depending on whether the slot is free
It is neither: what counts is how many model calls the system makes

items.stem:
Here is the core of an assistant:

messages = [question]
for step in range(6):
    reply = model(messages, tools)
    if reply.tool_call is None:
        break
    messages.append(run_tool(reply.tool_call))

In one run the model asks for check_calendar for Friday, reads the result, and then asks for check_calendar again for Saturday. Who decided that the second calendar check would happen: the code or the model? Answer with one word.

Every booking must check the student's training record, then the calendar, then book, in that order, every time; a skipped check once put an untrained student on the laser cutter. The sponsor's model budget is small. Which design is best for this path?

options.text: An agent with the three tools and a prompt that states the required order
An agent on a stronger model, because ordering steps is a judgment call
An agent allowed to skip any step it judges unnecessary, to save cost
A fixed workflow in which code runs the three steps in that order

items.stem: Every model call costs $0.01. A fixed workflow always makes 3 model calls per request. An agent version makes between 2 and 8 model calls per request, and its loop has a hard cap of 8. Over 500 requests, how much more can the agent cost than the workflow in the worst case, in US dollars?

Your code asks the model to label each question "manual" or "booking", then runs the fixed manual-search steps or the fixed booking steps for that label. A teammate says the model decides what happens next, so this is an agent. Who is right?

options.text: The code owns the control flow: the model only picks among paths you wrote in advance
The teammate: the model's label decides which steps run, so the model owns the control flow
Neither fully: the model and the code each own half of the control flow
The teammate, but only if the model used is large enough to be trusted with the choice

items.stem: A student asks: "Find any machine here that can cut 6 mm acrylic and book the earliest free slot this week." Which machines get checked, and how many calendar lookups are needed, depends on what the manuals return. Fixed workflow or agent for this request? Answer with one word.
